la:noun:kalendae.html:
Kălendae (Cal-;
v. the letter K), ārum, f.
root kal-, cal-; Gr. καλέω; Lat. calāre, clamo; cf. Müll.; prop., the day when the order of days was proclaimed; hence
, the Calends, the first day of the month: primi dies nominati Kalendae, ab eo quod his diebus calantur ejus mensis nonae a pontificibus, quintanae an septimanae sint futurae, l. l.; : sed heus tu, ecquid vides Kalendas venire, Antonium non venire?: litteras accepi datas pridie Kalendas Maias,on the last day of April,.—Interest was due on the first day of each month; hence: tristes Kalendae,: celeres,.—This reckoning of time was Roman only; hence: Kalendae Ausoniae,.—Prov.: ad Kalendas Graecas solvere, i. e. never, August. ap. .— The Kalends were sacred to Juno,; ; hence the first day of the year, Kalendae Martiae, was celebrated as a festival of married women, the Matronalia: dabat, sicut Saturnalibus viris apophoreta, ita per Kalendas Martias feminis,: Martiis caelebs quid agam Kalendis,: scis certe, puto, vestra jam venire Saturnalia, Martias Kalendas,; ; hence: femineae Kalendae = Kal. Mart.,: Kalendae Sextae,the Calends of June,: Kalendae Germanicae,the Calends of September, (cf.: in memoriam patris Septembrem mensem Germanicum appellavit,): Kalendae Januariae primae,of next January,; .—
Transf., a month: nec totidem veteres, quot nunc, habuere Kalendas,: intra septimas Kalendas,; ; .
